For Respondent: Mr. D.Nitin  JUDGMENT
Challenging the impugned award passed by the tribunal in MCOP.No.762 of 2016, the petitioners have preferred this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. The claimants are wife and son of deceased 1st claimant.

Due to which, the deceased sustained injuries on his head and all over the body, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
04/07/2025 01:36:36 pm ) for which he underwent treatment in the hospital.
Under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal seeking for payment of compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.
While the claim petition pending, he died on 18.07.2017 and subsequently, his legal heirs have contested the claim petition.

3.The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the respondent Transport Corporation.
Having come to such a conclusion, the Tribunal has fixed the compensation only for the injury as Rs.20,140/- together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

4. The learned counsel for appellants would argue that the deceased was died due to the injury sustained in the accident, but the Tribunal failed to take note of the said fact and also not appreciated Ex.P5 medical record, which shows the continuous treatment taken by the deceased for the injury sustained in the accident and nexus between the death as well as injury was proved.

Inspite of that, the tribunal had erroneously fixed the award only taking into consideration of the R.Chindhamani vs The Managing Director on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146172385/
2 injury sustained by deceased Rubit.

sentences.text: Hence, he prayed to set aside the award passed by the tribunal and prayed for enhancement of compensation.

5. The learned counsel for respondent Transport Corporation raised objections stating that before the Tribunal, there is no medical proof relied on by the claimants nor to show that the death was caused due to the injury sustained in the accident.
In fact, the accident was happened in the year 2015 and he died in the year 2017 subsequently.
Therefore, the Tribunal had rightly fixed the compensation only for the injury, which needs no interference.

6. Heard rival submissions of both learned counsel for appellants and respondent and perused the materials available on record.
7.

On perusal of records, it reveals that at the time of accident, deceased was aged about 25 years and he sustained grievous injury as per AR Copy Ex.P2 all over the body including head injury as well as other grievous injury.
Immediately, he was admitted in the Government Hospital, Salem and taken treatment and thereafter he was discharged.
But, subsequently for the injury sustained by him in the brain, he took treatment in the private hospital during August 2016.
As per the medical record Ex.P5, it reveals that the history of illness of victim Rubit shows that he was subsequently developed brain stem lesion.

He also had Lt facial parests, Lt. hemiparesis for which physiotherapy was given.
Neuro Surgeon opinion also obtained, wherein it shows that he was suggested to undergo MRI cranio vertebral junction, but he was not affordable and he was discharged at request.

So, the discharge summary issued by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 04/07/2025 01:36:36 pm ) hospital Ex.P5 reveals that multiple injuries are grievous in nature and he was also suggested for further treatment as per Neuro surgeon opinion, but he was not affordable to pay the amount and got discharged.

Thus, after the said accident, the deceased Rubit continuously taking treatment and since he was not able to go for surgery due to economic condition of the family, he was died subsequently without taking better treatment.
Therefore, due to the injury sustained in the said accident he died 1  years later and the same was proved by the claimants through Ex.P5.
But the Tribunal failed to take into consideration of the same.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is set aside .
8.In the light of the above discussion, the compensation awarded by the tribunal for fatal injury of 1st claimant, who died after filing of application is liable to be modified.
As the deceased said to be working as a tailor, he would have earned a sum of Rs.500/- per day, so, the notional income is fixed as Rs.15,000/-.
The age of deceased is 25 years.
Hence, the future prospects is fixed at 40% and multiplier is fixed at 18.
The deceased is having three legal heirs viz., wife and sons.
So, loss of consortium is fixed for his legal heirs 40% x 3 = Rs.1,20,000/-.
Funeral expenses is fixed at Rs.15,000/- and loss of estate is fixed at Rs.15,000/-.
Furthermore, while the deceased 1st claimant is crossing road, the accident was happened.
Hence, 10% of contributory negligence is fixed on his side.

Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is enhanced as follows:

Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the tribunal at Rs.9,36,792/- is enhanced to Rs.19,95,650/-.
Insofar as the enhanced compensation is concerned, the deficit court fee, if not paid, shall be paid by the claimants.

The other directions issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 04/07/2025 01:36:36 pm ) of payment of compensation remains unaltered.

The respondent Transport Corporation is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5% p.a.
from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.

11. On such deposit of the enhanced compensation amount now determined by this Court, the appellants 1 to 3 are entitled to share the amount proportionately as ordered by the Tribunal and the appellants 1 to 3 are permitted to withdraw the enhanced award amount along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.

As far as the share of minor appellants viz., 2nd and 3rd appellants are concerned, the same shall be deposited in any nationalised bank bearing fixed deposit scheme until the minor attains majority and the interest thereon shall be withdrawn by minor appellants' mother, once in three months.
12.In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
